Parties: which companies or people entered into this agreement
the names of the contracting parties
who is the buyer and who is the seller
Agreement Date: the date on which the agreement was signed
Effective Date: the date the agreement comes into force
from when does the contract start to apply
Expiration Date: the date the initial term ends
how long does the contract last before it expires
Renewal Term: automatic renewal or extension of the contract after the first term
for how long is the agreement renewed
does the term roll over unless someone objects
Notice Period To Terminate Renewal: how much advance notice is needed to stop the contract from renewing
deadline to give notice of non-renewal
Governing Law: which country's or state's law applies to the contract
choice of law and jurisdiction for disputes
where would a dispute be heard
Most Favored Nation: the customer gets the best price or terms offered to anyone else
Non-Compete: a party may not compete with the other party
restriction on operating in the same business or region
Exclusivity: one party must deal only with the other party
exclusive supplier or exclusive distributor arrangement
a party may not sell to or work with third parties
No-Solicit Of Customers: a party may not approach the other party's customers
ban on poaching clients or business partners
Competitive Restriction Exception: exceptions to the non-compete or exclusivity obligations
carve-outs from the restrictions on competing
No-Solicit Of Employees: a party may not hire the other party's staff
ban on recruiting or poaching employees and contractors
Non-Disparagement: a party may not say negative things about the other
obligation not to make disparaging statements
Termination For Convenience: ending the contract early without a reason by giving notice
can a party walk away from the agreement at will
Rofr/Rofo/Rofn: right of first offer or first negotiation before selling to others
a party gets the first chance to buy or license
Change Of Control: what happens if a party is acquired or merges with another company
consent or termination right when ownership of a party changes
Anti-Assignment: can the contract be transferred to someone else
consent needed before assigning the agreement to a third party
Revenue/Profit Sharing: splitting revenue or profits between the parties
royalties or a share of income paid to the other party
Price Restrictions: limits on raising or lowering prices
price caps or price freezes on the goods or services
Minimum Commitment: minimum purchase amount or minimum order quantity
the customer must buy at least a certain volume
Volume Restriction: extra fees or consent needed if usage goes above a threshold
limit on how much of the product or service can be used
IP Ownership Assignment: who owns the intellectual property that is created under the contract
work product or inventions are transferred to the other party
Joint IP Ownership: intellectual property owned jointly by both parties
shared ownership of jointly developed technology
License Grant: what licence rights are given to the other party
permission to use the software, trademark or technology
Non-Transferable License: the licence cannot be passed on to anyone else
restrictions on transferring or sublicensing the licence
Affiliate License-Licensor: licence that also covers the licensor's affiliates' intellectual property
rights granted by the licensor's group companies
Affiliate License-Licensee: licence extends to the licensee's affiliates or subsidiaries
group companies of the licensee may use the licensed rights
Unlimited/All-You-Can-Eat-License: licence with no cap on the number of users or copies
Irrevocable Or Perpetual License: a licence that cannot be revoked or taken back
Source Code Escrow: source code is deposited with a third party
release of the source code if the vendor goes bankrupt
Post-Termination Services: obligations that continue after the contract ends
transition assistance or wind-down support after termination
Audit Rights: can a party inspect the other party's books and records
Uncapped Liability: liability that has no upper limit
damages that are not limited for certain breaches
Cap On Liability: maximum amount a party can be liable for
limitation of liability and time limit for bringing claims
Liquidated Damages: a fixed sum payable if a party breaches the contract
termination fee or penalty for early exit
Warranty Duration: period during which defects must be fixed
Insurance: a party must carry insurance coverage
required insurance policies and minimum coverage
Covenant Not To Sue: a party promises not to bring a claim or challenge the other's intellectual property
agreement not to contest the validity of the other party's rights
Third Party Beneficiary: someone who is not a party can enforce the contract
